questions.problem:
A restaurant manager records the total time $20$ customers waited before they were seated. The results are presented in the table below. 

| Waiting time (minutes) | Frequency |
| --- | --- |
| $0\le x<10$ | $4$ |
| $10\le x<15$ | $6$ |
| $15\le x<20$ | $7$ |
| $20\le x<30$ | $3$ |

$$

$$

Assuming that the waiting times within each class interval are uniformly distributed, find an estimate of the mean waiting time $\overset{―}{x},$ rounded to **one decimal place**.

Rounded to one decimal place, $\overset{―}{x}≈$
{{field-1}} minutes.
questions.worked_solution:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, the mean can be estimated as follows:

$$
\overset{―}{x}≈\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{K}{f}_{i}\cdot {m}_{i}
$$

where

- ${f}_{i}$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

- ${m}_{i}$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class, and

- $n$ is the total number of observations.

To estimate the mean, we add columns to our table for the midpoints of each class and the products of the midpoints and frequencies.

| Waiting time (minutes) | ${f}_{i}$ | ${m}_{i}$ | ${f}_{i}\cdot {m}_{i}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0\le x<10$ | $4$ | $5$ | $20$ |
| $10\le x<15$ | $6$ | $12.5$ | $75$ |
| $15\le x<20$ | $7$ | $17.5$ | $122.5$ |
| $20\le x<30$ | $3$ | $25$ | $75$ |

$$

$$

Finally, we sum the values in the last column and divide by $20$ (the total number of observations).

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & ≈\frac{20+75+122.5+75}{20} \\  & =\frac{292.5}{20} \\  & ≈14.6\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the frequency table below for a continuous variable $x.$ The total number of observations is $n=15,$ and the estimated sample mean is $\overset{―}{x}≈23.$

| Range | Frequency $({f}_{i})$ |
| --- | --- |
| $0\le x<10$ | $2$ |
| $10\le x<20$ | $4$ |
| $20\le x<30$ | $4$ |
| $30\le x<40$ | $5$ |

$$

$$

Using the midpoint of each class interval to approximate all observations within that class, estimate the standard deviation ${\sigma }_{n},$ using $n$ as the denominator in the variance formula.

Rounded to one decimal place, ${\sigma }_{n}≈$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, we can estimate the variance by treating all observations within each class as though they were equal to the midpoint of that class. This gives

$$
{\sigma }_{n}^{2}≈\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{K}{f}_{i}\cdot ({m}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where

- ${f}_{i}$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

- ${m}_{i}$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class,

- $n$ is the total number of observations, and

- $\overset{―}{x}$ is the estimated mean, calculated using the class midpoints.

To find the variance, we add columns to our table for the midpoints of each interval, the squared deviations of the midpoints from the mean, and the products of the squared deviations and frequencies.

| Range | ${f}_{i}$ | ${m}_{i}$ | ${({m}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})}^{2}$ | ${f}_{i}{({m}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})}^{2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0\le x<10$ | $2$ | $5$ | $324$ | $648$ |
| $10\le x<20$ | $4$ | $15$ | $64$ | $256$ |
| $20\le x<30$ | $4$ | $25$ | $4$ | $16$ |
| $30\le x<40$ | $5$ | $35$ | $144$ | $720$ |

$$

$$

Then, we divide the sum of all the values in the last column by $15$ (the total number of observations):

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{n}^{2} & ≈\frac{648+256+16+720}{15} \\  & =\frac{1640}{15} \\  & ≈109.3333\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the estimated standard deviation is the square root of the estimated variance:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{n} & ≈\sqrt{109.3333}≈10.5\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
In this lesson, we'll learn how to estimate the mean and variance of grouped data sets. We motivate the discussion by considering an example.

To measure member engagement, a librarian recorded the time $30$ library members spent reading in the reading room. They present their results as a frequency table, shown below:

| Reading Time (minutes) | Frequency |
| --- | --- |
| $0 \leq x \lt 20$ | $5$ |
| $20 \leq x \lt 40$ | $10$ |
| $40 \leq x \lt 60$ | $8$ |
| $60 \leq x \lt 80$ | $7$ |

Notice that the librarian has divided the reading time data into four **classes** with a frequency associated with each class. This frequency table gives the following information:

- $5$ members spent between $0$ minutes (inclusive) and $20$ minutes (exclusive) in the reading room.

- $10$ members spent between $20$ minutes (inclusive) and $40$ minutes (exclusive) in the reading room.

- $8$ members spent between $40$ minutes (inclusive) and $60$ minutes (exclusive) in the reading room.

- $7$ members spent between $60$ minutes (inclusive) and $80$ minutes (exclusive) in the reading room.

In this example and throughout this lesson, we'll assume the underlying data is *continuous.* This means that for any given class, the time can be any real number within that class.

For example, consider the first class:

$$
0 \leq x < 20
$$

Since the data is continuous, $x$ can assume *any* real number in this interval. In other words, 

$$
x = 10.5\,\textrm{mins}, \qquad x = 2.14546\,\textrm{mins}, \qquad x = 3.141\,592\,654\ldots\,\textrm{mins},
$$

are all valid times.

tutorials.name: A Summary of Mean Estimation for Continuous Grouped Data
tutorials.problem:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, the mean can be estimated as follows:

$$
\overline x \approx \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^K f_i \cdot m_{i}
$$

where

- $f_i$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

- $m_i$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class, and

- $n$ is the total number of observations.

tutorials.name: A Worked Example
tutorials.problem:
Let's once again consider the data collected by the librarian, shown below.

| Reading Time (minutes) | $f_i$ | $m_i$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $0 \leq x \lt 20$ | $5$ | $10$ |
| $20 \leq x \lt 40$ | $10$ | $30$ |
| $40 \leq x \lt 60$ | $8$ | $50$ |
| $60 \leq x \lt 80$ | $7$ | $70$ |

Earlier, we found that 

$$
\overline{x}\approx 41.3333
$$

rounded to four decimal places. Also, we have $n=30$ observations, which equals the sum of the $f_i$ column.

Let's estimate the variance of this data set to one decimal place using the following formula:

$$
\sigma^2_n \approx \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^K f_i \cdot (m_{i} - \overline x)^2
$$

First, we calculate the deviations of each midpoint from the estimated mean, rounding to four decimal places.

| Reading Time (minutes) | $f_i$ | $m_i$ | $m_i - \overline x$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0 \leq x \lt 20$ | $5$ | $10$ | $-31.3333$ |
| $20 \leq x \lt 40$ | $10$ | $30$ | $-11.3333$ |
| $40 \leq x \lt 60$ | $8$ | $50$ | $8.6667$ |
| $60 \leq x \lt 80$ | $7$ | $70$ | $28.6667$ |

Next, we square each deviation:

| Reading Time (minutes) | $f_i$ | $m_i$ | $m_i - \overline x$ | $(m_i - \overline x)^2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0 \leq x \lt 20$ | $5$ | $10$ | $-31.3333$ | $981.7757$ |
| $20 \leq x \lt 40$ | $10$ | $30$ | $-11.3333$ | $128.4437$ |
| $40 \leq x \lt 60$ | $8$ | $50$ | $8.6667$ | $75.1117$ |
| $60 \leq x \lt 80$ | $7$ | $70$ | $28.6667$ | $821.7797$ |

Then, we multiply each squared deviation by the respective frequency:

| Reading Time (minutes) | $f_i$ | $m_i$ | $m_i - \overline x$ | $(m_i - \overline x)^2$ | $f_i\cdot (m_i - \overline x)^2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0 \leq x \lt 20$ | $5$ | $10$ | $-31.3333$ | $981.7757$ | $4908.8785$ |
